section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Imagine you are standing at a hospital billing counter at nine o'clock at night. The bill is four and a half lakh rupees, and your cashless claim, where the insurance company pays the hospital directly, has just been denied. We told this story in our last video.
visual: Episode 01 glimpses (tools/cut_glimpses.sh): g1_counter → g2_bill (₹4,50,000) → g3_denied (CASHLESS DENIED stamp), each with a FROM EPISODE 1 corner tag.
sound: Hospital room tone; logo bug from 0:02
pacing: Cold open, no music for 2 s

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Here is what you need to know from it. A cashless denial is not the end of your claim. You can pay the hospital, and claim the money back later. And if the company still says no, there is a four-step plan. Collect your papers. File for reimbursement and write to the grievance officer. Register on Bima Bharosa. And step four, the Insurance Ombudsman.
visual: Episode 01 glimpses on each step: g4_step1 (papers) → g5_step2 (GRO email, 14 days) → g6_step3_bima → g7_step4_cio; then the four-step staircase holds lower left with step 4 lit.

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: So you paid the bill from your pocket, collected your hospital papers, came home, and filed for reimbursement.
visual: F01 phone and card insert, PX15 rupee notes; F09 papers to keyboard match cut.

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Three weeks later, an email lands in your inbox.
visual: PX06/F01 phone in hand; an unbranded email slides in (SIMULATION, no insurer logo).

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Either the insurance company rejects your claim all over again... or worse, out of your four and a half lakh rupee bill, they approve just one lakh twenty thousand, and cut the remaining three lakh thirty thousand rupees.
visual: G01 Claim Deduction (amounts re-set to Episode 01's bill): total, approved part fills, the cut peels away in coral.

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: At that moment, many families think they only have two choices.
visual: A dim corridor splits into two doors (ILLUSTRATION).

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Choice one. Hire a lawyer, go to consumer court, and wait, often for a long time, for a verdict.
visual: Left door: F02 paper detail, case files stacking (no dusty five-year court graphic).

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Or choice two. Answer one of those ads for a private claim recovery service, which promises to fight your case, but some ask for twenty percent or more of the money they recover as their fee.
visual: Right door: F08 a hand signing an unbranded agreement; phone ad frame (SIMULATION, no real brand).

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Stop right there. Before you pick either door, there is a third one. Step four of that plan.
visual: Both doors dim; the lit step 4 of the staircase becomes a third door opening in teal light (ILLUSTRATION).
sound: Music out 1.5 s before, then a low thud

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Today, we open that door fully, from start to finish. Filing a complaint costs zero rupees. If the Ombudsman passes an award, it is binding on the insurance company. And if the company does not challenge the award, but pays it late, it has to pay you a penalty of five thousand rupees for every day of delay.
visual: G04 Binding Award panel reveal; S01 Rules p11 push-in on the award clause.
onscreen: FREE TO FILE [CIO FAQ] · AWARD BINDS THE INSURER [RULE 17] · ₹5,000 / DAY LATE [IRDAI HEALTH MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024]

en: Welcome to Be Practical with Kishore.
visual: Logo sting over F14 Hyderabad (faceless film, owner 2026-10-15).

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Today, I will show you one common mistake that gets complaints turned away at the door, how to file on the official website step by step, what happens at the hearing, and what the company must do after it loses. All without paying a single rupee to middlemen.
visual: Quick preview: RETURNED stamp, cioins.co.in typed, a hearing frame, the ₹5,000 meter (F09, F12, G06).

section: 1 The rejection email and the two doors
en: Let's break it down... in plain, simple English.
visual: Title card over F14.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: First... step three, Bima Bharosa, the online complaint portal of the insurance regulator, the I-R-D-A-I. It often works. But if it does not work for you, do not stop there.
visual: Staircase: step 3 lights; S07 Bima Bharosa home page push-in (the same capture as Episode 01).
onscreen: STEP 3 · bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in · 63% SETTLED FOR THE POLICYHOLDER, 2025–26 [IRDAI CONSULTATION PAPER | 2026]

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: You register on Bima Bharosa, upload your papers, and wait. Many people then get the same rejection letter from the insurance company again, and the complaint is closed.
visual: The same unbranded letter returns (SIMULATION); no fabricated portal screenshot.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: And you think, even the government portal could not help me.
visual: PX05 a man in a dim room, head in hand.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: Here is why. Bima Bharosa is useful. Your complaint goes on the regulator's record, and the company has to answer it. But Bima Bharosa is NOT a court. Your complaint goes to the same insurance company that cut your claim, and the I-R-D-A-I tracks how the company handles it. Bima Bharosa does not decide your claim, and it does not pass an order telling the company to pay you.
visual: Animated ticket travels from the phone to the insurer's inbox; an IRDAI tracker follows it (ILLUSTRATION).
onscreen: TRACKS · DOES NOT DECIDE [BIMA BHAROSA | IRDAI]

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: That is why step four exists. The body that can pass a binding award in your case... is the Insurance Ombudsman, which works under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, twenty seventeen.
visual: S03 FAQ → S01 Rules cover push-in, gold highlighter.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: Now, back to the second door. Private claim recovery companies.
visual: F08 agreement on a desk.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: Suppose your three lakh thirty thousand rupees is stuck. A recovery agency tells you, sign our agreement, and if we get your money back, give us twenty percent plus G-S-T.
visual: G02 Commission Example (re-set to ₹3,30,000): the claim strip.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: Twenty percent of three lakh thirty thousand is sixty-six thousand rupees. Add eighteen percent G-S-T, and it is seventy-seven thousand eight hundred and eighty rupees out of your family's medical savings.
visual: G02: fee splits off, GST joins last.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: And here is what they may not tell you. Under Rule fourteen of the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, the complaint is made by you, the person with the grievance, or through your legal heir, nominee or assignee.
visual: S01 Rules p9 crop to Rule 14(1), cyan overlay on the eligible complainants.

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: The form is the same free form on the official website that you can fill in yourself. And never share your passwords or O-T-Ps with anyone.
visual: F01 phone with a lock overlay (original graphic).

section: 2 Bima Bharosa, the Ombudsman and the middleman
en: So before you sign any agreement and give away a share of your money, remember. You can do this yourself online, for zero rupees.
visual: G02 the fee strip folds back into the family's money (ILLUSTRATION).

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Now listen carefully. You cannot jump straight to the Ombudsman on the day your claim is rejected.
visual: A closed glass door, the case file in hand (ILLUSTRATION).

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: If you do, your complaint can be turned away at the door.
visual: A red RETURNED stamp on a file (SIMULATION).

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: In twenty twenty-four to twenty-five alone, seventeen hundred and fifteen health complaints were turned away for this one reason. The person had not complained to the insurance company first.
visual: Files stack and bounce off the closed door (ILLUSTRATION); the CIO table H8 row under a magnifier.
onscreen: 1,715 HEALTH COMPLAINTS TURNED AWAY · NO COMPLAINT TO THE INSURER FIRST [CIO ANNUAL REPORT 2024–25 | STATEMENT H8]

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Under Rule fourteen, you must follow a two-step clock.
visual: G03 Process Clocks: two dials appear.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Clock step one. This is step two of our plan. Complain in writing to the insurance company, best of all to its Grievance Redressal Officer, the G-R-O.
visual: F09 typing; an illustrative email builds: policy number, claim number, amount, reason (invented numbers).

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Every insurer has to show its grievance officer's details on its website, and the Ombudsman's website lists their email addresses too. Send one calm, formal email with your policy number, your claim number, and why their deduction is wrong.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Keep a copy of that email and every reply. You will need them later.
visual: F07/F10 the email, the reply and the bills drop into one folder.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Under the I-R-D-A-I rules, the company should resolve your grievance within fourteen days.
visual: G03 first dial: fourteen days.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: Clock step two. Wait for their reply, or wait one month.
visual: G03 second dial: one month.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: The moment the company rejects your complaint, or you are not happy with its reply, or one month passes with no reply at all... the door to the Ombudsman opens.
visual: G03 two branches: unsatisfactory reply / no reply; the glass door opens.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: From that day, you have one year to file your complaint with the Ombudsman, for compensation of up to fifty lakh rupees.
visual: S01 Rules p9 (one year) then p11 (cap) as two separate crops.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: That limit was raised to fifty lakh rupees in November twenty twenty-three.
visual: Gazette page push-in.

section: 3 The two-step clock
en: And remember one strict condition. The Ombudsman cannot take your complaint if the same dispute is already pending, or already decided, in any court, consumer forum, or arbitration.
visual: S01 Rules p9 crop: pending OR disposed of.
onscreen: PENDING OR DECIDED ELSEWHERE = NOT ALLOWED [RULE 14(5)]

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: So, how do you actually file, and what happens next?

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Open your browser and go to the official website, c-i-o-i-n-s dot co dot in.
visual: G07 step 1, cioins.co.in typed (labelled schematic).

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Choose Register Complaint, and verify your mobile number with an O-T-P.
visual: G07 step 1 stepper; no real OTP shown.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Then you choose your Ombudsman office. There are eighteen offices across India, in cities like Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata. You pick the one that covers the place where you live, or the insurance company's branch that handled your policy.
visual: G08 Regional Offices board: Hyderabad lights first, then the rest (a directory board, not a map).

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Before you submit, keep these documents ready.
visual: G05 Document Checklist frame.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: One. A copy of your insurance policy.
visual: G05 document 1 flies into its slot.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Two. The hospital discharge summary and the itemised final bill.
visual: G05 document 2.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Three. The company's rejection or deduction letter.
visual: G05 document 3.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Four. A copy of the complaint you sent to the insurance company.
visual: G05 document 4.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: And five. Your I-D and address proof, and a photograph. Each file can be a P-D-F or a J-P-G, up to ten M-B.
visual: G05 extra slot; the portal's field list (credited capture).

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Check every detail, tick the declaration, and submit. Your complaint is verified first, and then registered. Save the acknowledgement and your complaint number.
visual: G07 step 4 review state; F10 saving the acknowledgement (no real complaint number).

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Now, what happens next?

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: The Ombudsman hears both sides, you and the company. The hearing can be in person, or online by video.
visual: F12 / PX13 hearing on a laptop, labelled; F11 detail.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Many complaints end in mediation under Rule sixteen. The Ombudsman suggests a fair settlement, and if both sides agree, the case closes. In twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, about one in three health complaints that were closed, ended this way.
visual: Two document cards slide together (ILLUSTRATION); S01 Rules p10 crop.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: If there is no settlement, the Ombudsman decides the case, and passes an award.
visual: G04 award panel; S01 Rules p11 award clause.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: You don't need fancy legal words. Explain your case simply. When did you buy the policy? Why were you in the hospital? And how much did the company cut?
visual: F07 / F19 hand crop over papers.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: And how long does it take? Of the health complaints the Ombudsman closed in twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, about eight out of ten were closed within three months.
visual: A calendar strip fills to three months; 8 of 10 files close.
onscreen: 8 IN 10 CLOSED CASES · UNDER 3 MONTHS [CIO ANNUAL REPORT | 2024–25]

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: And here is why this law is built for you.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: First. Under Rule seventeen, when the Ombudsman passes an award, it is binding on the insurance company.
visual: G04 insurer panel locks.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Wait... what if you are NOT happy with the award? You don't have to accept it. Other legal remedies, like the consumer forum, may still be open to you.
visual: G04 complainant panel: other remedies.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: And second. Under the I-R-D-A-I health master circular of twenty twenty-four, the insurance company must carry out the award within thirty days of receiving it.
visual: S01 Rules p11 / S06 FAQ crop; G06 receipt-date marker.
onscreen: 30 DAYS FROM RECEIPT [IRDAI HEALTH MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024]

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: If it is late, and it has not challenged the award within those thirty days, it must pay you a penalty of five thousand rupees for every day of delay, on top of any interest that is due.
visual: G06 Delay Penalty: deadline marker.
onscreen: ₹5,000 / DAY · NOT IF CHALLENGED IN 30 DAYS [IRDAI HEALTH FAQ 45 · POLICYHOLDERS' INTERESTS MASTER CIRCULAR | 2024]

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Ten days late, that is fifty thousand rupees. Thirty days late, one lakh fifty thousand rupees.
visual: G06 counter: 1, 10, 30 days late.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: And in December twenty twenty-four, the Bombay High Court heard the case of a senior citizen who had won an Ombudsman award, but was not paid for more than three years. The court ordered the insurance company to pay the award with interest, plus one lakh rupees in costs, and said the costs and interest should be recovered from the officers responsible, after an inquiry.
visual: Court exterior still with slow push (credited), judgment text crop.
onscreen: [BHARAT HIRJI DEDHIA v. UNION OF INDIA | BOMBAY HC | 2024]

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: That is the power of knowing your rights. You don't need connections, and you don't need to pay twenty percent to middlemen.
visual: F14 Hyderabad dusk.

section: 4 Filing, the hearing and the award
en: Be smart. Be informed. And always... be practical.
